text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- The stock market is growing sceptical of Aker RGI's chairman Kjell Inge Roekke and CEO Bjoern Rune Gjelsten following the poor first-half result of Norway Seafoods.
- A majority of voters dislike the close relationship between the Labour Party and the confederation of trade unions (LO), according to an opinion poll by MMI.
- SAS CEO Jan Stenberg surprised the stock market with strong first-half results and the share price rose sharply.

- Oslo Bourse demands a full explanation from Norway Seafood regarding the company's result for the first half of 1997. Norway Seafood, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, said on Tuesday it had taken a provision in the first-half accounts of 400 million crowns for restructuring costs.
- Oil and Energy Minister Ranveig Froeiland plans to invest in expanding hydro-electric power in the next few years.
- The three centrist parties will stop the construction of one of two natural gas power plants now being planned should they win the September 15 election, the Centre Party says.
